title: Climate Evidence: From Australia's Power System to Global Temperature Records
summary: Surface temperature, satellite observations, atmospheric CO₂ and the electricity mix form a chain from measured climate change to practical response.
key_takeaway: Surface thermometers, satellites and atmospheric CO₂ measurements share almost nothing in common except their conclusion: independent instruments, different physics, and they still converge on a warming climate under rising greenhouse-gas concentrations. Uncertainty at the margins of any one record does not erase agreement at the centre of all of them. The electricity mix is where that evidence turns into a measurable, actionable lever for response.

inline_figures.caption: A curved fit to the global surface-temperature anomaly record highlights acceleration rather than a constant linear drift.
AIRS satellite temperature anomalies from 2002–2025 show a positive fitted trend despite substantial year-to-year variation.
Cape Grim measurements show carbon-dioxide concentration rising across decades while the normal annual seasonal cycle continues.
The NSW fuel mix shows renewable supply growing inside an electricity system that still depends heavily on thermal generation.
